analysis:
This batch is documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md gains the v0.10.7 candidate section (patch hunk head 11-413; the supplied units are historical v0.8.x and v0.5.0 tail text, lines 3959-4638, which are unchanged context), and eight changelog.d fragments are removed (they are folded into the changelog). No executable code, protocol, crypto, attestation, authorization or storage logic is changed in the supplied units, so no threat-model control is weakened.

What I read in the removed fragments and the changelog:
- The App Attest restart fragments describe a restart through launchd, driven by 'app-attest-verified.json' evidence (7-day window, one automatic restart per 6 hours). That evidence is local and does not grant serving authorization, consistent with T-052/T-053 (A-015/A-016) as I read them. The implementation is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm that app-attest-verified.json is not used as a trust source. The App Attest entitlement log line stays local and is not sent to the coordinator (T-058).
- The cluster auto-update fragment describes staged, verified downloads, a 30-second '--version' probe and rollback. That touches the update/rollback trust area (T-043, T-013), but the code is outside this batch.
- The equal tensor-parallel shares fragment is a functional fix with no new trust boundary.
- The checkpoint encoder/decoder fragments describe performance work on prefix-cache checkpoints with the same bytes and the same refusals. They preserve T-041 posture, and I could not verify them without the code.

Remaining questions for integration: whether the code behind the v0.10.7 notes (pair update coordination, App Attest restart) is covered by other batches. The CHANGELOG head hunk for lines 11-413 was not supplied as a numbered unit, so I did not review it. No findings.
